issue_title: fix(a11y): correct public schedule Grid semantics
problem_statement:
fix(a11y): correct public schedule Grid semantics

The owner-requested browser audit on 2026-09-14 found existing accessibility failures in the public schedule's Grid view. This is independent of #2030 (track descriptions).

Reproduction at ATA release c2a5565444cf48790cb3d5fa9589e5f59b5810ca:

1. Visit `https://events.allthingsai.org/events/all-things-ai-2026/schedule`.
2. Select Grid and All Tracks.
3. Run axe-core against the main content with WCAG2A/2AA/2.1AA tags at 1440px and 390px.

Observed: `aria-required-children` on the schedule grid and `aria-required-parent` on track column headers/grid cells. Both recur after deployment at runtime `74f9dd9`. Default Table Lighthouse scores accessibility 100, so a default-route-only Lighthouse check misses these interaction states.

Source scope for investigation: `src/app/(public)/events/[eventSlug]/schedule/schedule-board-view.tsx`. Preserve layout, filtering, keyboard navigation, and deep links. Use either a valid complete ARIA grid hierarchy/interaction model or suitable simpler semantics; do not suppress axe findings. Validate actual rendered Grid after filter/day changes on desktop and mobile, with a regression test that switches out of Table.

An initial 390px scan also flagged the selected All Tracks pill for `color-contrast` shortly after interaction; the post-deployment scan did not reproduce it. No filter CSS changed. Treat steady-state contrast as unconfirmed and remeasure after transitions settle before proposing any color changes.

Baseline evidence is in the originating task's `outputs/Schedule-Track-Descriptions/hosted-before/verification.json` and Grid screenshots. These findings predate #2030 and are not caused by the new guide; no schema, data, auth, or provider changes are implicated.
